acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: deploy/cron.nbshiyan sends a per-minute POST to old mail-queue -> existing mail gate/Bearer -> worker. After restart, controlled SMTP actually consumes committed mail. Keep stale/sent/failed/deferred/dropped fields unchanged and do not trigger through GET prefetch (E-94). 2) Compatible GET/POST entries share leases/JobState summaries. HTTP timeouts do not automatically replay or change methods to probe. Unknown SMTP outcomes preserve old unknown_delivery semantics. Unauthorized/disabled calls send no mail, and failure never claims SENT (E-35, E-41).

E-35.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-35.trigger: An email notification fails or is not connected.
E-35.expect: Represent the actual notification state using the defined queued/sending/sent/failed states or their existing DTO mapping. Notification failure after a message is saved changes only that notification state, not the message's received state or the inbox's ability to process it. An unconnected source must not display Sent.

E-41.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-41.trigger: A message has been saved but an operator reply or notification fails to send.
E-41.expect: Keep the received result and inbox pending-work state. Separately show the real sending failure; do not pretend that the visitor has been contacted.

E-94.trigger: An account without chat permission calls an outbox/notification endpoint, or the SMTP adapter can send only the existing inquiry format.
E-94.expect: Separately verify unauthorized calls are rejected and chat-notifications uses a dedicated restricted adapter without expanding the old mail UI. deploy/cron.nbshiyan must actually register a once-per-minute schedule, and committed outbox records must be consumed after restart; manual invocation alone or an empty future registration is insufficient. M4 registers the job with its delivery; M7 performs only final acceptance.
